extracted.intended_audience: bioscience authors and reviewers considering submission to EMBO Reports
extracted.subtask_description: Defines EMBO Reports' editorial scope, article-format expectations, and select peer-review/publishing policies (concise research reports with one key finding; Science & Society commentaries; policies on preprints, peer review transparency, and data curation). Useful for authors preparing manuscripts and reviewers assessing fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific quality beyond novelty and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: "EMBO Reports stands for scientific quality beyond narrow definitions of novelty and impact"," with a scope that embraces the biosciences from biophysics to ecology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis is on scientific quality rather than only novelty or perceived impact; suitable submissions can come from across the biosciences (example disciplines explicitly include biophysics to ecology).

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Short and sweet' research reports (single key finding)
rubrics_metrics.description: "'Short and sweet' research reports - a single key finding, backed up by multiple lines of experimental evidence. Comprehensive mechanistic insight is not required.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should be concise and focused on a clear, single result supported by multiple independent lines of experimental evidence; authors need not provide exhaustive mechanistic detail to be appropriate for the format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of confirmatory, refuting, and null studies
rubrics_metrics.description: "EMBO Reports invites well-developed studies that either confirm or refute prominent claims in the literature, as well as null data on important, open questions in the biosciences.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal explicitly welcomes rigorously conducted studies that validate, contradict, or report null results for important questions—importance and quality of study design/evidence are the deciding factors rather than novelty alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science & Society article standard — authoritative commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: "Science & Society: authoritative commentary examining the wider issues, challenges, and impacts at the intersection of research and society.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pieces in this section should provide authoritative, well-argued perspectives on broader societal, ethical, policy, or conceptual implications of research rather than narrow technical results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent and consultative peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: "Author benefits: ... transparent and consultative peer review, pre-decision and revision author discussion",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal practices a transparent and consultative approach to peer review, including opportunities for authors to discuss matters with editors before a decision and during revision, indicating an expectation of constructive, dialog-based review processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint scooping protection policy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posting a manuscript as a preprint does not constitute being scooped for the purposes of consideration at EMBO Reports (policy intended to protect authors who post preprints).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data-integrity and curation services expectation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal provides services focused on data integrity and curation, signaling an expectation that submitted work will meet standards for accessible, well-curated, and verifiable data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical scope — biosciences from biophysics to ecology
rubrics_metrics.description: "with a scope that embraces the biosciences from biophysics to ecology.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts should fall within the broad biosciences remit of the journal; this range of disciplines describes the journal's topical suitability criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness metric — rapid first decision
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal's median time to first decision is 5 days, indicating an operational expectation of rapid editorial handling and an author-facing metric for review speed.
